goals.title: Yellow River breach: relief and repair

messages.body: Narrow the channel. Once the dykes stand, the current carries the silt away for good. Diversion lets the bed silt up, and within ten years it breaks again.
Diversion is cheaper and works this year. Narrowing costs twice as much; I doubt we can pay for it.
Earlier reigns tried diversion again and again, and it failed every time. Narrowing needs strict checks on the dykes to stop corner-cutting.
@Works @Revenue You disagree. Works says diversion breaks again in ten years; Revenue says there isn't silver for narrowing. Answer each other.
@Works Narrowing is costed at 800,000 taels. Revenue can release 400,000 at most this year. Where does the rest come from?
@Revenue Diversion saves this year's silver. When it breaks again in ten years, closing it will cost far more than 800,000. Under Jiajing we diverted three times, and it broke three times.
@Revenue The Jiajing cases Works cites are accurate. Whatever diversion saves now will be repaid twice over.
@Works Revenue has only 400,000 taels this year. Can narrowing wait a step, so we do what's urgent this year first?

We can give ground: this year close the breach and build the inner dykes for 240,000 taels; the outer dykes next year. Add spillway dams at the dangerous stretches to release floods, which takes the best of diversion.
At 240,000 taels this year, Revenue can pay. We'll raise next year's dyke silver separately. Agreed.
The compromise works; no new objections. With the dykes built over two years, corner-cutting is likeliest in the second, so the inspection should check the dykes specifically.

process.note: Consensus: Narrow the channel; close the breach and build the inner dykes this year, the outer dykes next year, spillway dams at dangerous stretches; cost spread over two years; disagreements: No real disagreement once Works gave ground; the Censorate asks for a dedicated dyke inspection
